previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, chronic systolic heart failure with an ejection fraction of 25%, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and productive cough. He presented with orthopnea and low oxygen saturation. Imaging revealed pulmonary edema and a right lung opacity suggestive of pneumonia. He was treated with IV furosemide for heart failure exacerbation and broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to levofloxacin for bacterial pneumonia. His respiratory status improved, and he became afebrile with resolving radiographic findings. Diuresis was paused due to rising creatinine, and he was discharged on oral furosemide with instructions to monitor weight and follow up on kidney function. Blood cultures and respiratory viral panels were negative.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr ___ is a ___ year old man with a history of AML M5b s/p 
double cord transplant (___) complicated by GVHD and 
systolic CHF (EF ___ in ___ presenting with acute nausea, 
vomiting, diarrhea, and fevers. 

#VOMITING, DIARRHEA, and FEVERS:
Patient presented with acute nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, 
with fevers following potential exposure to family with 
gastroenteritis. Symptoms were consistent with gastroenteritis.  
During his admission, he had frequent watery diarrhea. When he 
was not taking any PO food or fluids, diarrhea stopped, 
consistent with malabsorptive process rather than 
secretory/inflammatory diarrhea.  He was treated empirically for 
bacterial gastroenteritis with cipro/flagyl, completing a 6 day 
course. Rotavirus stool antigen positive on the day following 
discharge; all other stool studies for infectious diarrhea were 
negative, including C diff and norovirus. Blood and urine 
cultures were negative.   On admission, he was hypotensive, and 
he was resuscitated with IV crystalloid, with increasing UOP and 
down-trending creatinine.  After several days of observation, 
there was less concern for bacterial infection, and so he was 
started on loperamide and psyllium wafers, as well as 
cholestyramine.  On discharge, he was still having loose stools, 
but ___ episodes per day, greatly decreased from admission, and 
he was able to tolerate bland foods.  He was discharged with 
supply of loperamide, psyllium, and cholestyramine and 
instructed to continue these medications until diarrhea 
decreased. 

#HYPOTENSION and ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY: 
Shortly after arrival at ___, patient noted to be hypotensive 
to 88mmHg systolic. There were no changes in patient's symptoms 
at this time, no chest pain or pre-syncope or shortness of 
breath.  Most likely cause based on history (vomiting, diarrhea, 
inability to tolerate PO) and exam (dry oral mucosa, lack of 
pulmonary rales or lower extremity edema) suggested etiology of 
hypovolemia with distributive hypotension due to fevers.  
Bicarbonate was low on on admission, with creatinine elevated 
above recent baseline.  Anion gap was only mildly elevated 
relative to the degree of decrease in the bicarbonate, and so 
the predominant process was felt to be NAGMA, due to GI losses 
of bicarbonate.  VBG indicated moderately severe acidosis, with 
pH 7.13. Patient responded moderately well to 500cc fluid 
boluses and maintenance fluids with bicarb, with improvement in 
pH and serum bicarbonate, and down-trending creatinine with 
increased UOP. 

#DYSPNEA and SYSTOLIC CHF:
EF ___ in ___. Patient required fluid resuscitation due to 
hypovolemia, hypotension, and metabolic acidosis with acute 
kidney injury.  He was given maintenance fluids after initial 
fluid resuscitation, and on hospital day 3 developed dyspnea, 
orthopnea, with pulmonary rales and chest XR demonstrating 
pulmonary edema. Echo ___ largely unchanged from one year 
ago with LVEF 25%. He was diuresed with intravenous furosemide 
with improvement in dyspnea and pulmonary exam.  On the day 
prior to discharge, he was weaned off of supplemental O2. His 
metoprolol was restarted at home dose. He was continued on home 
dose aspirin.
